DEATH IN THE INNER CITY

By: Latashia Naidoo | Commission

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
DJ Warras wanted to fix crime in Joburg’s inner city. Instead, he ended up a victim of it.

Unique Selling Point:
New information has emerged over the murder and targeted attacks.

Summary:
On 16 December 2025, DJ Warras (Warrick Stock) was shot dead in broad daylight outside Zambezi House in Johannesburg’s CBD.
There is no publicly released CCTV footage of the shooting.
What is known comes from police statements, court records, and eyewitness accounts.
DJ Warras was not performing or socialising, he was working - involved in security-related operations linked to hijacked buildings - spaces widely recognised as operating under organised criminal control.

This investigation examines what was known before the killing, including documented threats and multiple protection orders, what protection existed in practice, and how the case is now unfolding as it enters court.
It situates DJ Warras’ death within two overlapping realities: the largely hidden violence surrounding hijacked buildings, and the reality of organised crime in Joburg’s inner city.

With new on-record information emerging about a hijacked-buildings intervention blueprint under development at the time of his death, and the case returning to court on 06 January, 2026, the story interrogates risk, protection and accountability while the record is still being written.

Press Release:


Death in the Inner City
He wanted to fix crime in Joburg’s inner city; instead, he became its victim. Last month, media personality Warrick Stock, better known as DJ Warras, was shot dead in broad daylight in Johannesburg’s CBD. But what does his murder say about the long arm of organised crime in our economic capital? Stock was helping to develop a blueprint for intervention in the city’s hijacked building crisis… and it seems his work brought him into the firing line. As the story unfolds in court, Carte Blanche paints a picture of risk and threat, and asks: will anyone be held accountable for this tragic death?
Producer: Latashia Naidoo | Presenter: Govan Whittles


Script:


DEATH IN THE INNER CITY - FINAL

WARRICK STOCK: “Town is f**king dangerous, it’s heavy… they grip all four of your limbs, take your stuff, and if you fight, they stab you. And they los you there, and nobody does anything.”

NEWS AUDIO: “Breaking news story this hour: a popular DJ has been shot and killed in the Johannesburg CBD.”

NEWS AUDIO: “At this point we understand it is DJ Warras.”

NEWS AUDIO: “DJ Warras has in fact been shot and killed.”

(PAUSE)

VO: “It was a brutal daylight murder - in the middle of Joburg’s inner city.”

(PAUSE)

VO: “Outside a building under siege.”

CHAD THOMAS: “Maybe he was overconfident. He didn’t understand just how dangerous this industry is.”

BEVERLEY STOCK: “For me, everything has been taken away. They took away my child, every, every thing.”

VO: “Was it a case of being at the wrong place at the wrong time… or an assassination linked to his work at a hijacked building?”

FTB.

VO: “This is Johannesburg’s inner city.”

VO: “Once the engine of the economy, it’s now characterised by urban decay, hijacked buildings, and a criminal ecosystem.”

WARRICK STOCK: “Whad’up, it’s Warras, the Shady Lurker. Welcome to a special edition of the Shady Phodcast.”

VO: “Podcaster and former radio DJ Warrick Stock, known as DJ Warras, spoke openly about inner-city crime.”

VO: “Off-air, he was involved in efforts to reclaim hijacked buildings.”

WARRICK STOCK: “We do a lot of work in the CBD, because I’ve got a security company as well, and essentially what we do is we come into like a hijacked building and we look at - we do like a building audit if you will. Like who’s hijacked the building, who’s staying in the building. You know, because you’ll find like the…”
SIAS DU PLESSIS: ‘It’s dangerous work though bud…’
WARRICK STOCK: “Little bit. But I’m a dangerous oke, Sias, geez.”
SIAS DU PLESSIS: “The Shady Lurker.’

VO: "Zambesi House, opposite the popular Carlton Centre, was one of those buildings.”

VO: “Through a security company he owned, Warrick was contracted to manage access, formalise rentals, and restore basic order at the hijacked property.”

VO: “It ran alongside his life in entertainment - a world whose dangers those closest to him didn’t fully understand… Until the 16th of December last year, when he was murdered in broad daylight.”

(PAUSE)

VO: “This is Warrick’s mother, Beverley Stock.”

GOVAN: ‘Did you know that he was looking at hijacked buildings and getting them back?’
BEVERLEY STOCK: “I did, but I didn’t know the dangers that were involved, I really didn’t. I mean, Warrick turned 40 in November, and one of the conversations we had is that: ‘You’re 40 years old now, the boys are getting bigger, you need to be more safe.”

VO: “She’s speaking publicly for the first time about the death of her only child - and a family history marked by violence.”

BEVERLEY STOCK: “His Dad died when he was 8 years old. He was shot in Krugersdorp in 1994 in his jugular, so he died within minutes. And isn’t it just really so profound that the same thing has happened to Warrick?”

BEVERLEY STOCK: “I haven’t yet had time to actually accept that Warrick is gone forever. So what I do every evening is go back and look at videos of him…
GOVAN: “On the Whatsapp chats…”
BEVERLEY STOCK: “... listen to voicenotes, and just try and accept that he is no more. But I’m a little bit scared because besides the day of the incident, and the memorial and funeral, I haven’t really cried.”

VO: “Warrick was shot five times. One of the bullets struck his face.”

BEVERLEY STOCK: “I just kept thinking this, this loving person has been reduced to an urn of ash. That’s very, very difficult for a mother to get their head around…”

VO: “Beverley says Warrick didn’t speak about the dangers at Zambesi House. This voicenote was sent in September last year, soon after he started working there.”

WARRICK STOCK VOICENOTE: “But I was in town, Mom, at Marshalltown by the building, there’s a crisis there. City of Joburg has turned off the water… The toilets are overflowing, the shit is spilling everywhere. And then today is also the first day of our security deployment… starting tonight we’ll have guards on duty for the nightshift and whatever, whatever, so that just occupied my morning..”

VO: “Zambesi House stands among hundreds of other hijacked buildings in the Joburg CBD.
Privately owned and managed through a trust, it houses hundreds of residents across multiple storeys.
For years, control of the building has been contested.
Nearly half of those living here are believed to be non-paying occupants.”

VO: “The building was already in crisis when Warrick stepped in.”

VO: “Arnie Williams was part of that team.”

GOVAN LINK: “We’re about to meet up with the security that Warrick was working with, to save the hijacked buildings. We’re here where he was shot. They’re going to take us inside Zambesi House. Hey, Arnie.
ARNIE WILLIAMS: ‘Hello sir.’
GOVAN: “Good, thank you man. Ya, let’s go inside.”

ARNIE WILLIAMS: “So that fingerprint system got active two days before Warrick got shot.”
GOVAN: “Is this building safe right now?”
ARNIE WILLIAMS: “I wouldn’t, I wouldn’t believe so, no. How can it be safe now cos this door is standing open?”
GOVAN: ‘Well, we’re with you. So let’s, let’s go in I think.’

GOVAN: “It smells like meat. What’s down here?”
ARNIE WILLIAMS: “There’s a butchery.”
GOVAN: “In the Zambesi Building basement?”
ARNIE WILLIAMS: “In the Zambesi Building basement, there’s a butchery.”

VO: “It’s a health and safety nightmare. Arnie says waste from the illegal butchery isn’t being disposed of through approved systems - it’s fed into air ducts designed to ventilate the building.”

ARNIE WILLIAMS: “This here is an oil trap. They’re running it through an air duct - have a look at this pipe here. Can you see this?”
GOVAN: ‘It’s run through the air duct?’
ARNIE WILLIAMS: “Have a look at that.”

GOVAN LINK: “DJ Warras came into this hijacked building, and set up access control. He immediately clashed with the syndicate that’s running this building. And that may have cost him his life.”

VO: “Warrick had a plan - a blueprint to reclaim Zambesi House.”

ARNIE WILLIAMS: “Firstly, you gotta take back control. How do you take control? You shutter down on the access points: guards, biometric systems - all the stuff that Warrick has implemented here was the right way to do it. You cannot fix a building if you don’t have control over a building.”

GOVAN: “But he was killed. Why was he killed?”
ARNIE WILLIAMS: “The reason Warrick would’ve been killed is because he stopped access to the illegal people.”
VO: “On the 16th of December last year, Warrick arrived at Zambesi House to oversee the installation of CCTV cameras. Police believe he was called outside and ambushed while walking to his car.”
GOVAN LINK: “This is the spot where Warrick was killed. He had left the building and was walking to his car when he was approached by the gunman. He was shot five times, and ran towards the building - where his body was found. The gunman has since been arrested - or so they say.”

VO: “In fact, six days after the murder, this man - Victor Majola - was arrested in connection with Warrick’s killing.”

VO: “Police say footage from nearby CCTV links him to the shooting.”

VO: “But, as we suspected, by the time of broadcast, the actual triggerman was still at large.”

(PAUSE)

VO: “We obtained CCTV footage from outside Zambesi House. It shows Majola and the alleged gunman before and after the attack. The shooting itself is not captured.”

VO: “Investigators believe Majola’s girlfriend lives at Zambesi House.”
VO: “This investigation keeps circling back to one thing: hijacked buildings - and the power structures inside them.”
GOVAN LINK: “Hijacked buildings hide in plain sight, but they operate outside of the law. They generate income, act as a haven for criminals, and are often defended. So disputes over buildings like these are rarely just about property.”

VO: “Warrick knew the risks.”

WARRICK STOCK: “The police can’t catch a cold, so they don’t go in and stop what’s happening in those buildings. Because 9 times out of 10 there’s a slum lord in charge of that building who pays a bribe, and the police leave him alone, right.”

VO: “Because of that danger, some of the people who worked alongside him can’t be identified.
Wiseman was part of Warrick’s security team here.”

WISEMAN: “Warrick arrived here around half past 9 and they shot him around 12, ya.”
GOVAN: “So you think, you think the people who called the killers stay here?”
WISEMAN: “Yes.”
GOVAN: “You think they’re here right now?”
WISEMAN: “Yes.”

GOVAN LINK: “This is the centre of the hijacked building. We have security, but I can’t shake this feeling that we’re being monitored. We are being watched. There are people that have come down now, sitting on the stairs, and they weren’t here before.”
VO: “At Zambesi House, Warrick’s work had started to name names.”
VO: “He and his team identified residents who weren’t paying rent - and in the weeks before his death, he applied for protection orders against some of them.”
WISEMAN: “You see… This is the list of the people that are not paying the rent… We were in a process to register everyone. Everyone must bring a valid ID and stuff. Two days after, that’s when he was shot.”
GOVAN: ‘Did he ever tell you that he felt unsafe? That he was scared for his life?’
WISEMAN: “No, he never said that. But you know coming to Zambesi alone, he used to tell me: ‘You know what my brother, I can’t go there alone. I don’t trust those people.’

VO: “Despite being a relative newcomer, Warrick appeared to recognise the risks of working in hijacked buildings.”
VO: “Security expert Chad Thomas has experience and has operated in the sector since the 1990s.”
CHAD THOMAS: “Johannesburg has been in a state of decay for many years now… to the point where parts of Johannesburg are just completely under the control of, of gangs and guys with a nefarious agenda.”

GOVAN: “Who’s controlling these hijacked buildings in the inner city?”
CHAD THOMAS: “So a lot of people would be quick to say foreign nationals - and they would be wrong. The foreign nationals live in those buildings. Whereas in actual fact there’s a lot of South Africans sitting behind all of this.”

VO: “In hijacked buildings, illegal landlords make money from illegal tenants able to access the properties. Warrick was trying to put a stop to that at Zambesi House.”

CHAD THOMAS: “I don’t know whether it’s about the fact he was interfering in somebody's revenue flow, or whether it was the fact that they thought ‘if this guy takes a foothold in our industry, because of his network and because he’s so well known, he can become a massive problem for us.”

VO:“Warrick took precautions. They weren’t enough.”
VO: “On the day he was killed, he arrived at Zambesi House armed - but without security.”
CHAD THOMAS: “The working theory is that a group of bad actors
who had control of part of the building wanted to maintain that control. And therefore took him out.”

VO: “As the case moves through the courts, Warrick’s family are left to carry the loss.”

BEVERLEY STOCK “What I used to say to him: ‘You fly too close to the sun, and you’re gonna get your wings burnt.’”
GOVAN: “Hey, that’s how a Mummy talks, hey. That’s exactly what a mother would say.”
BEVERLEY STOCK: “Yes, and when this happened I just said yes, he got his wings permanently burnt this time.”

VO: “He leaves behind three young sons.”

VO: “Before his death, Warrick began work to fix what’s broken in the inner city. That work continues, despite the risk.”

CHAD THOMAS: “Sadly, Warras was one of those wakeup calls that people needed - to show them that nobody is safe in South Africa.”

VO: “DJ Warras’ story ends here. But the fight for Johannesburg’s inner city goes on.”

WARRICK STOCK: “Yeah man, you know the story: take it easy, and if it’s easy take it home.”

FTB.

PROMOS:

PROMO 1:

VO: “Inner-city crime. A public execution. And the cost of speaking out.”

CHAD THOMAS: “Sadly Warras was one of those wakeup calls that people needed - to show them that nobody is safe in South Africa.”

BEVERLEY STOCK: “Really for me, Warrick’s death just feels like it’s the end. There’s nothing to… everything has been taken away. They took away my child, every, every thing.”

VO: “We unpack how power, profit, and violence collide in Johannesburg’s inner city.”

PROMO 2:

VO: “How did a well-known DJ and podcaster become the target of a brutal daylight killing in Joburg’s inner city?”

CHAD THOMAS: “I don’t know whether it’s about the fact he was interfering in somebody's revenue flow, or whether it was the fact that they thought ‘if this guy takes a foothold in our industry, because of his network and because he’s so well known, he can become a massive problem for us.”

VO: “We unpack the sinister forces at play behind the city’s hijacked building crisis.”

PROMO 3:

VO: “A public killing - linked to money, territory, and power.”

CHAD THOMAS: “So the working theory is that a group of bad actors who had control of part of the building, wanted to maintain control. And therefore took him out.”

VO: “Who really controls Johannesburg’s hijacked buildings - and what happens when that control is challenged?”

But I’m a dangerous oke, Sias, geez.” SIAS DU PLESSIS: “The Shady Lurker.’ VO: "Zambesi House, opposite the popular Carlton Centre, was one of those buildings.” VO: “Through a security company he owned, Warrick was contracted to manage access, formalise rentals, and restore basic order at the hijacked property.” VO: “It ran alongside his life in entertainment - a world whose dangers those closest to him didn’t fully understand… Until the 16th of December last year, when he was murdered in broad daylight.” (PAUSE) VO: “This is Warrick’s mother, Beverley Stock.” GOVAN: ‘Did you know that he was looking at hijacked buildings and getting them back?’ BEVERLEY STOCK: “I did, but I didn’t know the dangers that were involved, I really didn’t. I mean, Warrick turned 40 in November, and one of the conversations we had is that: ‘You’re 40 years old now, the boys are getting bigger, you need to be more safe.” VO: “She’s speaking publicly for the first time about the death of her only child - and a family history marked by violence.” BEVERLEY STOCK: “His Dad died when he was 8 years old. He was shot in Krugersdorp in 1994 in his jugular, so he died within minutes. And isn’t it just really so profound that the same thing has happened to Warrick?” BEVERLEY STOCK: “I haven’t yet had time to actually accept that Warrick is gone forever. So what I do every evening is go back and look at videos of him… GOVAN: “On the Whatsapp chats…” BEVERLEY STOCK: “... listen to voicenotes, and just try and accept that he is no more. But I’m a little bit scared because besides the day of the incident, and the memorial and funeral, I haven’t really cried.” VO: “Warrick was shot five times. One of the bullets struck his face.” BEVERLEY STOCK: “I just kept thinking this, this loving person has been reduced to an urn of ash. That’s very, very difficult for a mother to get their head around…” VO: “Beverley says Warrick didn’t speak about the dangers at Zambesi House. This voicenote was sent in September last year, soon after he started working there.” WARRICK STOCK VOICENOTE: “But I was in town, Mom, at Marshalltown by the building, there’s a crisis there. City of Joburg has turned off the water… The toilets are overflowing, the shit is spilling everywhere. And then today is also the first day of our security deployment… starting tonight we’ll have guards on duty for the nightshift and whatever, whatever, so that just occupied my morning..” VO: “Zambesi House stands among hundreds of other hijacked buildings in the Joburg CBD. Privately owned and managed through a trust, it houses hundreds of residents across multiple storeys. For years, control of the building has been contested. Nearly half of those living here are believed to be non-paying occupants.” VO: “The building was already in crisis when Warrick stepped in.” VO: “Arnie Williams was part of that team.” GOVAN LINK: “We’re about to meet up with the security that Warrick was working with, to save the hijacked buildings. We’re here where he was shot. They’re going to take us inside Zambesi House. Hey, Arnie. ARNIE WILLIAMS: ‘Hello sir.’ GOVAN: “Good, thank you man. Ya, let’s go inside.” ARNIE WILLIAMS: “So that fingerprint system got active two days before Warrick got shot.” GOVAN: “Is this building safe right now?” ARNIE WILLIAMS: “I wouldn’t, I wouldn’t believe so, no. How can it be safe now cos this door is standing open?” GOVAN: ‘Well, we’re with you. So let’s, let’s go in I think.’ GOVAN: “It smells like meat. What’s down here?” ARNIE WILLIAMS: “There’s a butchery.” GOVAN: “In the Zambesi Building basement?” ARNIE WILLIAMS: “In the Zambesi Building basement, there’s a butchery.” VO: “It’s a health and safety nightmare. Arnie says waste from the illegal butchery isn’t being disposed of through approved systems - it’s fed into air ducts designed to ventilate the building.” ARNIE WILLIAMS: “This here is an oil trap. They’re running it through an air duct - have a look at this pipe here. Can you see this?” GOVAN: ‘It’s run through the air duct?’ ARNIE WILLIAMS: “Have a look at that.” GOVAN LINK: “DJ Warras came into this hijacked building, and set up access control. He immediately clashed with the syndicate that’s running this building. And that may have cost him his life.” VO: “Warrick had a plan - a blueprint to reclaim Zambesi House.” ARNIE WILLIAMS: “Firstly, you gotta take back control. How do you take control? You shutter down on the access points: guards, biometric systems - all the stuff that Warrick has implemented here was the right way to do it. You cannot fix a building if you don’t have control over a building.” GOVAN: “But he was killed. Why was he killed?” ARNIE WILLIAMS: “The reason Warrick would’ve been killed is because he stopped access to the illegal people.” VO: “On the 16th of December last year, Warrick arrived at Zambesi House to oversee the installation of CCTV cameras. Police believe he was called outside and ambushed while walking to his car.” GOVAN LINK: “This is the spot where Warrick was killed. He had left the building and was walking to his car when he was approached by the gunman. He was shot five times, and ran towards the building - where his body was found. The gunman has since been arrested - or so they say.” VO: “In fact, six days after the murder, this man - Victor Majola - was arrested in connection with Warrick’s killing.” VO: “Police say footage from nearby CCTV links him to the shooting.” VO: “But, as we suspected, by the time of broadcast, the actual triggerman was still at large.” (PAUSE) VO: “We obtained CCTV footage from outside Zambesi House. It shows Majola and the alleged gunman before and after the attack. The shooting itself is not captured.” VO: “Investigators believe Majola’s girlfriend lives at Zambesi House.” VO: “This investigation keeps circling back to one thing: hijacked buildings - and the power structures inside them.” GOVAN LINK: “Hijacked buildings hide in plain sight, but they operate outside of the law. They generate income, act as a haven for criminals, and are often defended. So disputes over buildings like these are rarely just about property.” VO: “Warrick knew the risks.” WARRICK STOCK: “The police can’t catch a cold, so they don’t go in and stop what’s happening in those buildings. Because 9 times out of 10 there’s a slum lord in charge of that building who pays a bribe, and the police leave him alone, right.” VO: “Because of that danger, some of the people who worked alongside him can’t be identified. Wiseman was part of Warrick’s security team here.” WISEMAN: “Warrick arrived here around half past 9 and they shot him around 12, ya.” GOVAN: “So you think, you think the people who called the killers stay here?” WISEMAN: “Yes.” GOVAN: “You think they’re here right now?” WISEMAN: “Yes.” GOVAN LINK: “This is the centre of the hijacked building. We have security, but I can’t shake this feeling that we’re being monitored. We are being watched. There are people that have come down now, sitting on the stairs, and they weren’t here before.” VO: “At Zambesi House, Warrick’s work had started to name names.” VO: “He and his team identified residents who weren’t paying rent - and in the weeks before his death, he applied for protection orders against some of them.” WISEMAN: “You see… This is the list of the people that are not paying the rent… We were in a process to register everyone. Everyone must bring a valid ID and stuff. Two days after, that’s when he was shot.” GOVAN: ‘Did he ever tell you that he felt unsafe? That he was scared for his life?’ WISEMAN: “No, he never said that. But you know coming to Zambesi alone, he used to tell me: ‘You know what my brother, I can’t go there alone. I don’t trust those people.’ VO: “Despite being a relative newcomer, Warrick appeared to recognise the risks of working in hijacked buildings.” VO: “Security expert Chad Thomas has experience and has operated in the sector since the 1990s.” CHAD THOMAS: “Johannesburg has been in a state of decay for many years now… to the point where parts of Johannesburg are just completely under the control of, of gangs and guys with a nefarious agenda.” GOVAN: “Who’s controlling these hijacked buildings in the inner city?” CHAD THOMAS: “So a lot of people would be quick to say foreign nationals - and they would be wrong. The foreign nationals live in those buildings. Whereas in actual fact there’s a lot of South Africans sitting behind all of this.” VO: “In hijacked buildings, illegal landlords make money from illegal tenants able to access the properties. Warrick was trying to put a stop to that at Zambesi House.” CHAD THOMAS: “I don’t know whether it’s about the fact he was interfering in somebody's revenue flow, or whether it was the fact that they thought ‘if this guy takes a foothold in our industry, because of his network and because he’s so well known, he can become a massive problem for us.” VO:“Warrick took precautions. They weren’t enough.” VO: “On the day he was killed, he arrived at Zambesi House armed - but without security.” CHAD THOMAS: “The working theory is that a group of bad actors who had control of part of the building wanted to maintain that control. And therefore took him out.” VO: “As the case moves through the courts, Warrick’s family are left to carry the loss.” BEVERLEY STOCK “What I used to say to him: ‘You fly too close to the sun, and you’re gonna get your wings burnt.’” GOVAN: “Hey, that’s how a Mummy talks, hey. That’s exactly what a mother would say.” BEVERLEY STOCK: “Yes, and when this happened I just said yes, he got his wings permanently burnt this time.” VO: “He leaves behind three young sons.” VO: “Before his death, Warrick began work to fix what’s broken in the inner city. That work continues, despite the risk.” CHAD THOMAS: “Sadly, Warras was one of those wakeup calls that people needed - to show them that nobody is safe in South Africa.” VO: “DJ Warras’ story ends here. But the fight for Johannesburg’s inner city goes on.” WARRICK STOCK: “Yeah man, you know the story: take it easy, and if it’s easy take it home.” FTB. PROMOS: PROMO 1: VO: “Inner-city crime. A public execution. And the cost of speaking out.” CHAD THOMAS: “Sadly Warras was one of those wakeup calls that people needed - to show them that nobody is safe in South Africa.” BEVERLEY STOCK: “Really for me, Warrick’s death just feels like it’s the end. There’s nothing to… everything has been taken away. They took away my child, every, every thing.” VO: “We unpack how power, profit, and violence collide in Johannesburg’s inner city.” PROMO 2: VO: “How did a well-known DJ and podcaster become the target of a brutal daylight killing in Joburg’s inner city?” CHAD THOMAS: “I don’t know whether it’s about the fact he was interfering in somebody's revenue flow, or whether it was the fact that they thought ‘if this guy takes a foothold in our industry, because of his network and because he’s so well known, he can become a massive problem for us.” VO: “We unpack the sinister forces at play behind the city’s hijacked building crisis.” PROMO 3: VO: “A public killing - linked to money, territory, and power.” CHAD THOMAS: “So the working theory is that a group of bad actors who had control of part of the building, wanted to maintain control. And therefore took him out.” VO: “Who really controls Johannesburg’s hijacked buildings - and what happens when that control is challenged?”

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): DJ Warras wanted to fix crime in Joburg’s inner city. Instead, he ended up a victim of it.
metadata.Unique Selling Point: New information has emerged over the murder and targeted attacks.
metadata.Summary: On 16 December 2025, DJ Warras (Warrick Stock) was shot dead in broad daylight outside Zambezi House in Johannesburg’s CBD. There is no publicly released CCTV footage of the shooting. What is known comes from police statements, court records, and eyewitness accounts. DJ Warras was not performing or socialising, he was working - involved in security-related operations linked to hijacked buildings - spaces widely recognised as operating under organised criminal control. This investigation examines what was known before the killing, including documented threats and multiple protection orders, what protection existed in practice, and how the case is now unfolding as it enters court. It situates DJ Warras’ death within two overlapping realities: the largely hidden violence surrounding hijacked buildings, and the reality of organised crime in Joburg’s inner city. With new on-record information emerging about a hijacked-buildings intervention blueprint under development at the time of his death, and the case returning to court on 06 January, 2026, the story interrogates risk, protection and accountability while the record is still being written.
